hero.title: 10 Best Street Food Spots in Adelaide
hero.dek: The best street food in Adelaide — curated from local food blogs, Adelaide Central Market vendors, and r/Adelaide. Falafel, dumplings, oysters, Korean street food, and more. Interactive map included.

intro.answerFirst: Adelaide isn't just Australia's wine capital — it's quietly become one of the country's best cities for street food. The Adelaide Central Market, operating since 1869, forms the beating heart of the city's food culture, housing over 70 vendors under one roof.
body: Beyond the market, you'll find Korean street food tucked into CBD laneways, late-night Chinese on Gouger Street, and Lebanese shawarma in the western suburbs. Adelaide's multicultural heritage — Greek, Italian, Vietnamese, Lebanese, and increasingly Korean — has created a diverse street food landscape that rivals Sydney and Melbourne at a fraction of the price.

We analyzed food blogs, local guides, and recommendations from the Adelaide food community including r/Adelaide to build this list. Each spot was verified for current hours and quality as of April 2026.
intro.methodology: We analyzed local food blogs, Broadsheet Adelaide, Glam Adelaide, and recommendations from the Adelaide food community including r/Adelaide, cross-referencing with Google ratings and recent reviews. Each pick was verified for current hours, quality, and menu accuracy as of April 2026.

picks.name: Real Falafel
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Consistently ranked Adelaide's best falafel. Fresh, fast, and affordable.
picks.whatToOrder: Classic falafel wrap with all the toppings — hummus, tabouleh, pickles, tahini.
picks.insiderTip: Quick, affordable, and authentic Middle Eastern street food
picks.bestFor: Quick, affordable, and authentic Middle Eastern street food
picks.limitations: Queues during peak market hours · Limited seating

redditQuotes.quote: Real Falafel is a must-visit at the Central Market. Get there early on Saturday to avoid the crowds.

picks.name: Samtass Seafoods
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Adelaide's go-to for fresh oysters. Expert shucking, local produce.
picks.whatToOrder: Half dozen SA oysters — try them plain, or with seaweed and Thai dressing.
picks.insiderTip: Fresh oysters and premium SA seafood at market prices
picks.bestFor: Fresh oysters and premium SA seafood at market prices

faq.question: What is Adelaide's best street food market?
faq.answer: The Adelaide Central Market is Australia's largest undercover produce market and the heart of Adelaide's street food scene. Operating since 1869, it houses over 70 vendors selling everything from fresh oysters and falafel to Korean dumplings and Italian pizza. Best times to visit are Friday evenings and Saturday mornings.

faq.question: Where can I find Korean street food in Adelaide?
faq.answer: Adelaide has a thriving Korean street food scene. Top spots include Daebak Brothers on Compton Street for fried chicken and tteokbokki, Mandoo on Bank Street for handmade dumplings, and Plus 82 Pocha on Grenfell Street for authentic pocha-style Korean dishes and fried chicken.

faq.question: What's the best cheap eat at Adelaide Central Market?
faq.answer: Real Falafel offers some of the best value — freshly made falafel wraps for under A$12. Lucia's Pizza & Spaghetti Bar has affordable pasta and pizza slices. For a quick snack, CocoCane's fresh sugarcane juice is refreshing and budget-friendly at around A$6-8.

faq.question: What are the Adelaide Central Market opening hours?
faq.answer: Adelaide Central Market is open Tuesday 7am-5:30pm, Wednesday 9am-5:30pm, Thursday 9am-5:30pm, Friday 7am-9pm (late night shopping), and Saturday 7am-3pm. The market is closed Sunday and Monday. Individual vendors may have slightly different hours.

faq.question: Where can I get fresh oysters in Adelaide?
faq.answer: Samtass Seafoods at Adelaide Central Market has a dedicated oyster bar serving freshly shucked South Australian oysters. They're available Friday evenings and Saturday mornings, served plain or with accompaniments like seaweed, caviar, or Thai dressing. Expect to pay around A$3-4 per oyster.

faq.question: Is Adelaide good for food tours?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Adelaide is consistently ranked among Australia's best food cities. The Adelaide Central Market offers guided food tours, and Gouger Street (Chinatown) is perfect for self-guided street food crawls. The city's compact layout makes it easy to hit multiple spots in one day.

faq.question: What's the best time to visit Adelaide for street food?
faq.answer: Friday evenings are ideal — the Central Market stays open until 9pm with a vibrant atmosphere. Saturday mornings (7am-11am) offer the freshest produce and busiest energy. For Gouger Street late-night eats, weekends after 10pm deliver the authentic experience.

faq.question: How much should I budget for street food in Adelaide?
faq.answer: Adelaide street food is excellent value. Budget A$10-15 for a filling meal at most vendors. A falafel wrap runs A$10-12, dumplings A$12-18, and a dozen oysters around A$36-40. A full street food crawl sampling 4-5 spots typically costs A$40-60 per person.
